correctness.rationale: For each two-image deterministic map \(F\), the channel is CPTP by the Kraus family \(K_j=|F(j)\rangle\langle j|\). Its traceless Weyl block is derived explicitly and has nonzero entries only between the two diagonal Weyl operators. The packaged exact checker exhausts all eighteen such maps and all \(216\) projective qutrit Clifford adjoint actions in \(\mathbb Q(\omega)\), proves the averaged \(64\times64\) block is rational, and verifies its rank, distinct-root annihilating polynomial, and trace. Those identities determine all multiplicities. Wallman--Flammia Eq. (89) makes the full \(81\)-dimensional second-moment operator block lower triangular; its one-copy scalar is \(f_F=(r-1)/8\), obtained from the superoperator trace. The resulting three spectra all have unique unit-modulus eigenvalue \(1\) and largest nontrivial modulus \(1/6\). The proof also directly shows the unital projection has a negative diagonal output entry \(-1/3\) on a positive basis projector, so it is not positive.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete exact classification for the natural two-image deterministic classical qutrit family in the smallest dimension not covered by the source's qubit corollary. It covers all eighteen nonunital maps, identifies full eigenvalue multiplicities, and gives the uniform largest nontrivial modulus \(1/6\). The family is structurally relevant because its unital projection is nonpositive, so it exercises precisely the obstruction that prevents the source's higher-dimensional argument, and the qutrit Clifford design is used in experimental randomized benchmarking.
